themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Explode
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting a sudden emergence of a new or intensifying neighborhood issue around street-level dining operations.
evidence: 3 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Timing aligns with spring season when outdoor dining expands
reporting_angles: Have restaurants illegally expanded outdoor seating? Are sidewalks being obstructed?
Are residents complaining about noise, waste, or congestion tied to outdoor dining?
Is the city enforcing outdoor dining permits and regulations in Crown Heights?

themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facility Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints jumped to 15 THIS WEEK versus a 4.1-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 264% spike (z-score: 5.21)—indicating a potential crisis in park, building, or public facility upkeep.
evidence: 15 maintenance complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.1 weekly average
Z-score of 5.21 indicates high statistical anomaly
Community Board has repeatedly requested park building reconstruction funding, suggesting chronic facility neglect
reporting_angles: Which specific parks or facilities are generating the spike in complaints?
Are residents reporting broken equipment, poor conditions, or safety hazards in public spaces?
Is the city's maintenance backlog worsening as spring brings more park usage?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Spike 2 Weeks Ago
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 14 TWO WEEKS AGO compared to a 2.9-complaint weekly average—a 387% spike (z-score: 5.18)—suggesting either a coordinated tagging campaign or deteriorating code enforcement in the district.
evidence: 14 graffiti complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Spike occurred 2 weeks ago; verify if complaints have subsided or continue this week
reporting_angles: Was there a specific tagging crew or organized graffiti campaign in Crown Heights 2 weeks ago?
Has the Parks Department or NYPD responded to the spike?
Are anti-graffiti cleanup efforts keeping pace with the problem?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints jumped to 6 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 1.0-complaint weekly average—a 500% spike (z-score: 4.47)—pointing to potential organized tree removal or vandalism in the neighborhood.
evidence: 6 illegal tree damage complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly average
Z-score of 4.47 indicates statistically significant spike
Community Board has requested park building and tree infrastructure upgrades, suggesting environmental neglect concerns
reporting_angles: Who is illegally removing or damaging trees? Residents, contractors, or city work?
What species and how many trees were damaged during the 2-week spike?
Is Parks Department investigating unauthorized tree removal or is there a pattern of permit violations?

themes_detail.label: Electrical Issues Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a 0.4-complaint weekly average—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—suggesting potential electrical infrastructure problems or building code violations in the district.
evidence: 3 electrical complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
472 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (283 alterations), suggesting renovation activity that may be generating electrical issues
reporting_angles: Are contractors performing electrical work without proper permits or inspections?
Are residents reporting dangerous electrical hazards, outages, or code violations?
Is the spike tied to the high volume of building alterations being filed with DOB?
